candidates.title: Prepare travel and purchase request checklists

demandEvidence.chore: Administer travel bookings and purchases by preparing a reviewable request checklist from supplied details.

ease.reason: A beginner can mock an intake-to-checklist flow; n8n documents moving and transforming data across apps, but not a travel or purchasing connector.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a professional office may value less request handling; this paid role does not establish AI buyers or willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A two-week prototype can structure operator-supplied fictional requests into a review checklist; booking rules and real-system access are unknown.

autonomy.reason: A trigger can organize supplied requests and draft a checklist; staff must verify details and authorize every booking or purchase.

evidence.reason: The fresh notice explicitly names travel bookings and purchasing, but gives little detail on frequency, inputs or constraints.

candidates.reason: Concrete paid administrative work supports a narrow proposed intake and checklist experiment, but the independent scores average 5.2, below the threshold; no post proposed. The workflow must not book or purchase automatically.

rejected.title: Prepare travel and purchase request checklists
rejected.reason: This bounded checklist experiment is below the equal-weight threshold (mean 5.2); n8n only documents generic data movement/transformation, and human authorization remains necessary for bookings and purchases.

rejected.title: Paid administrator role
rejected.reason: The privacy-safe notice contains no concrete task excerpt, only an administrator role. Do not invent duties from the title; it cannot support a scoped demand-first proposal.

steps.message: Assessed both selected professional-services demand leads. The travel-booking and purchasing notice supports a narrow checklist experiment, but its evidence-limited mean is below 6; the other notice has no concrete task. No post proposed.
